panels.title: LMCache configured in-flight submits per initiator

panels.description:
InRdmaWrites increments when an NVMe-oF READ is satisfied by the target RDMA-writing into initiator memory. It is a TRANSACTION counter, not a byte counter, and it is valid as a traffic-shape gate only.

MEASURED ON FALCON 2026-08-12 across all 20 cells of the remote_xfs read sweep: bytes per InRdmaWrite is stable within a block size (+/-0.3% across reps) but varies 13x ACROSS block sizes -- 3,523 B at bs=4k, 14,004 at 16k, 38,991 at 144k, 45,073 at 256k, 45,084 at 512k, saturating near 45 KB. So no fixed ops-to-bytes constant is valid, and the 52,428 B segment cap documented for the RoCE path does NOT hold here. Never compare this rate across block sizes.

For bytes use the ethtool fabric-throughput panel or ACC telemetry (bytes_from_ulp_rc for writes, bytes_to_ulp for reads).
panels.title: RDMA operations — read path (target→initiator) [DIAGNOSTIC]

panels.description:
InRdmaReads increments when an NVMe-oF WRITE makes the target RDMA-read from initiator memory. Transaction counter, shape gate only -- see the read-path panel for why no generic byte conversion is valid on Falcon. Payloads <= 4 KiB ride in-capsule (OutRdmaSends only) and register zero RDMA read operations.

This stays near zero for read-only sweeps; that is correct, not a gap.
panels.title: RDMA operations — write path (initiator→target) [DIAGNOSTIC]

panels.description:
Wire-level fabric throughput on the Falcon plane, and the primary throughput instrument on this rig.

CALIBRATED 2026-08-12 against ib_write_bw at a known 96.05 Gb/s sustained for 70 s: port-tx-bytes tracked payload at ratio 1.0347, i.e. payload plus 3.5% wire framing, and the five 10 s sample means averaged 99 Gb/s. The counter is accurate.

USE A >=60s WINDOW. Shorter windows alias badly: the same sustained 96 Gb/s load rendered as 85.28 / 99.58 / 100.20 / 111.89 / 98.54 Gb/s across consecutive 10 s samples, and 111.89 is above the negotiated 100 GbE link. That is the sampling artifact behind the historical '208 Gb/s' reading, not a defect in the counter. The NIC updates port counters in bursts, so a short window can enclose two updates or none.

Note the driver spells these inconsistently -- port-rx_bytes but port-tx-bytes -- which the collector's gsub normalizes to port_rx_bytes / port_tx_bytes. Read rx on the initiator (mkp1) and tx on the target (mkp2): an NVMe-oF read is the target writing into initiator memory.
panels.title: Fabric throughput — ethtool port counters (>=60s window)

panels.description:
irdma names xon/xoff events rather than mlx5's *_pause_phy. Nonzero xoff means the link is asserting backpressure.

WINDOW WIDENED TO 60s 2026-08-12. This metric comes from a node_exporter TEXTFILE collector, so its value is stale between collector writes while Prometheus keeps scraping at 5 s. Measured over a 2-minute idle range query, consecutive scrapes returned delta 0 (a repeated stale read) directly adjacent to ~1.5 GB jumps. A short rate window that happens to span a stale sample followed by a jump reports a spike: under a sustained, verified 96.05 Gb/s load, consecutive 10 s samples read 85.28 / 99.58 / 100.20 / 111.89 / 98.54 Gb/s -- and 111.89 is above the negotiated 100 GbE link. Their mean, 99 Gb/s, is correct. Note node_disk_* metrics are NOT affected: they are read directly by node_exporter, not via a textfile, so shorter windows remain valid there.

panels.description: Completed I/Os per second on the target's own PM9A3 devices. Pair with the throughput panel above to read back the effective I/O size the target actually sees (Bps / IOPS), which is what tells you whether the initiator's 144/256/512 KiB request survived the fabric intact or was split.
panels.title: Target SSD IOPS (mkp2 NVMe)

panels.description:
Fabric-side request rate on the imported NVMe-oF namespaces, plus the md0 RAID0 above them. md0 counts the striped request while the namespaces count the per-leg requests, so md0 is roughly the sum of its legs, not a duplicate.

DEVICE SELECTION FIXED 2026-08-12. This panel previously matched `device=~"nvme2n1|nvme3n2"`. On mkp1 the imported namespaces are actually nvme0n1 and nvme3n1: `nvme3n2` has never existed, and `nvme2n1` is a LOCAL idle PM9A3, so the panel plotted an idle local drive and a nonexistent device instead of the fabric. Kernel NVMe names are not stable across reboots, so selection is now by the `nvme_namespace_role` metric emitted by nvme_stats_textfile.sh (role="imported" == has no pcie transport, carries the target's subsystem NQN) rather than by hardcoded name.
panels.title: Initiator IOPS (mkp1 imported namespaces + md0)

panels.description:
iostat's r_await / w_await: total per-request wait divided by completions, so it INCLUDES queueing, not just service time. At saturation await rises with offered depth while throughput stays flat — that is the queue growing, not the device slowing, and it is the signature to look for when comparing QD16 against QD32 cells.

Gaps are real: the ratio is undefined when a device completes no I/O in the window, which is exactly what happens between sweep cells.
panels.title: Target SSD await (mkp2)

panels.description:
Initiator-side await on the imported namespaces. The difference between this and the mkp2 await panel is the fabric plus target-stack cost of one request: if initiator await climbs while target await stays flat, the added delay is on the transport or in the target's queues, not in the media.

panels.title: Initiator await (mkp1 imported namespaces + md0)

panels.description:
Fraction of wall time with at least one I/O in flight (iostat %util). On a multi-queue NVMe device this saturates at 1.0 long before the device is out of capacity -- one outstanding request is enough to pin it -- so 100% here does NOT mean the drive is the bottleneck.

panels.description: Intel PCM samples DRAM-controller bandwidth for one second every five seconds. This is host-wide DRAM traffic, not NVMe-oF payload bandwidth. Use it to identify a target-memory or cross-socket pressure limit after storage and fabric counters have been checked.
panels.title: PCM DRAM bandwidth by socket

panels.description: Kernel node-local MemUsed. This is a host-memory pressure indicator, not a measure of the benchmark process's allocation or registered memory alone.
panels.title: NUMA node memory used

panels.description: Kernel node-local allocation counters. `local_node` is an allocation satisfied on the requesting node; `other_node` is an allocation satisfied elsewhere. These counters are host-wide, so correlate their change during a timed cell rather than attributing their absolute value to LMCache.
panels.title: NUMA local vs other-node allocations

panels.description: `numa_miss` means an allocation could not be satisfied on its preferred node. `numa_foreign` is the reciprocal accounting view. Both are kernel-wide counters; a rise during a cell is diagnostic evidence, not proof that the benchmark alone caused it.
panels.title: NUMA misses / foreign allocations
